subject: MSA: proposal for OEM module indemnity and evidence-handback
messages:
From: Emma Cole <emma.cole@meditech.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@meditech.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MSA: indemnity carveouts for OEM modules

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending over the redline. Two items on indemnity we need clarified so procurement can sign off:

1) Scope: we need the supplier indemnity to cover third-party claims alleging infringement arising out of the supplied software AND any OEM-integrated modules that rely on our provided SDKs or embeddings.
2) Remedies: we expect supplier to control defense for covered claims and provide indemnity for damages and settlement, subject to customary notice and cooperation terms.

Please let me know whether Redwood can accept language that covers OEM modules where Meditech is the integrator, and whether you can commit to the usual defense-control mechanics. If you prefer a carveout (e.g., for open-source components or customer-provided data), list them explicitly.

I attached a short note from procurement on acceptable evidence and timeline expectations.

Thanks,
Emma Cole
Senior Counsel, Legal Operations
Meditech Systems
Attachments: evidence_requirements_meditech.pdf (PDF)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA: indemnity carveouts for OEM modules

Ben / Kim,
Forwarding Emma's note — Meditech wants broader indemnity that specifically names OEM-integrated modules that use our SDKs/embeddings. Procurement expects us to accept defense control and damages for covered claims.

Commercial context: this is a ~$1.1M annual committed Dedicated deal, close to signing if we can resolve this quickly. Sam (cc'd on Emma's original) is pushing for execution next week.

Questions for Kim: can we accept third-party IP claims that include OEM modules so long as we narrow to allegations traceable to Redwood code or model weights? Any recommended carveouts (OSS, customer-provided prompts/data)?

Ben — need your view on whether we offer a concession (cap/escrow or insurance waterfall) to keep the commercial intact.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA: indemnity carveouts for OEM modules

Quick take: this is a close-won opportunity and Meditech will walk if their legal team perceives open risk on OEM modules. Commercially I'd prefer to accept defense-control mechanics with reasonable limits, e.g.:

- Redwood to indemnify for third-party IP claims only where the claim arises solely from Redwood-delivered code, model weights, or proprietary runtime (not customer code or training data).
- Exclude open-source components and clearly exclude customer-supplied data/prompt engineering that could create risk.
- Offer a $2M cap per claim / $4M aggregate OR accept defense + indemnity subject to insurance offset (we expect them to carry insurance too).

If legal can draft a short indemnity snippet with the exclusions above, I can present to Sam and push for a 48-72 hour signoff.

-Ben
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA: indemnity carveouts for OEM modules

Laura / Ben — see my read below and attached draft snippets. High level: we can accept defense-control for covered claims but need to narrow the trigger and preserve standard OSS/customer-data carveouts. Proposed solution (short form):

- Trigger: Redwood shall indemnify Meditech for third-party claims solely to the extent such claims arise from (i) Redwood proprietary model weights, (ii) Redwood-delivered runtime binaries, or (iii) code authored and delivered by Redwood as part of the Agreement.
- Exclusions: No indemnity for claims resulting from (a) customer modifications, (b) third-party/OSS components not modified by Redwood, or (c) any customer-provided training data or prompts.
- Remedies: Redwood may elect to assume defense with counsel reasonably acceptable to Meditech; if Redwood assumes defense, settlements requiring payment must not include injunctive relief without Redwood's consent.
- Cap: Propose $2M per claim / $4M aggregate, with an insurance-first waterfall (apply Redwood commercial insurance before Redwood pays from balance).
- Evidence & notice: Meditech must provide prompt written notice, a complete copy of the claim, and the technical reproduction steps where available; we propose a 30-day cure/triage window for technical investigation before payment.

Attachments: Indemnity_snippet_proposal.txt (text) — includes redline snippets for MSA Section 9 (Indemnification) and an Evidence_List_Template.pdf for procurement to complete.

If Ben is comfortable, I can send this as our formal counter to Emma with the redline attached.

-Kim
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Cole <emma.cole@meditech.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@meditech.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed compromise: indemnity trigger + evidence-handback (MSA redline attached)

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short counterproposal from Redwood that aims to bridge procurement's position and what we can accept operationally. Key points:

- Narrowed trigger: indemnity limited to claims arising from Redwood proprietary model weights, runtime, or Redwood-delivered code (explicitly excludes customer modifications and OSS).
- Defense mechanics: Redwood may assume defense; we propose reasonable-counsel approval and a prohibition on settlements imposing injunctive obligations without Redwood consent.
- Cap & insurance: $2M per claim / $4M aggregate + insurance-first waterfall.
- Evidence-handback: we included a short Evidence_List_Template that Meditech can fill to speed triage. We ask Meditech to provide reproduction steps and any available logs. Redwood will triage within 30 days and propose remediation or defense strategy.

Attachments: MSA_meditech_redline_20280328.docx (DOCX), Indemnity_snippet_proposal.txt (TXT), Evidence_List_Template.pdf (PDF)

We believe this resolves the material concerns while limiting our retrospective exposure. Ben will follow up on commercial concession language (if any) after you confirm the redline is acceptable. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Cole <emma.cole@meditech.com>

Subject: Re: Proposed compromise: indemnity trigger + evidence-handback (MSA redline attached)

Laura,

Appreciate the quick, pragmatic counter — that articulation of triggers and the evidence template helps procurement and legal. A couple of follow ups:

- We need to confirm the $2M/$4M numbers with finance — likely acceptable but will revert.
- On the 30-day triage: procurement asks that critical PII/data exposures be triaged faster; can Redwood commit to an expedited path for incidents flagged as data exposure?

Sam will coordinate on the call — propose tomorrow at 10:00am PT. If that works for Redwood folks, we will share a short internal memo to finance/legal before the call.

Thanks — talk tomorrow.
Emma
Senior Counsel, Meditech Systems
